summary: U.S. equity markets traded mixed on Tuesday as major banks kicked off third-quarter earnings season while semiconductor stocks extended a five-day losing streak. Goldman Sachs beat expectations with revenue of $18.68 billion and earnings of $17.01 per share, sharply above consensus, while Wells Fargo missed on revenue despite beating on earnings. Johnson & Johnson shares plunged 5-6% after missing adjusted earnings estimates. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 1.2-1.5%, marking a 17% decline from its June record as concerns mount over Chinese chipmaker CXMT's advances in memory technology. Oil remained elevated above $105 per barrel on Middle East tensions, while the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 5.22%. Investors are bracing for critical September CPI data due Wednesday morning at 8:30 AM ET, with consensus expecting 3.6-3.7% year-over-year inflation, up from August's 3.4%. Bitcoin slipped below $82,000 amid $771 million in liquidations and $681 million in weekly ETF outflows. The Fed's next rate decision is October 28, with market-implied odds of a hike sitting near 16-19% after weak September payrolls data shifted expectations toward December.

signals.title: Semiconductor selloff deepens on China competition fears
signals.desc: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 1.5% Tuesday, extending losses to 17% from June highs as reports of Chinese chipmaker CXMT's memory chip advances raise competitive concerns.

signals.title: Major banks deliver mixed earnings as Goldman beats, Wells misses
signals.desc: Goldman Sachs crushed estimates with $18.68B revenue and $17.01 EPS versus $12.90 consensus, while Wells Fargo missed revenue by $450M despite beating earnings; Citigroup also topped estimates.

signals.title: Bitcoin drops below $82K on $771M liquidations and ETF outflows
signals.desc: Bitcoin fell 2.8% to $81,382 amid $771 million in leveraged position liquidations and $681 million in net weekly Bitcoin ETF outflows as traders await Wednesday's CPI print.

signals.title: Oil holds above $105 on Middle East geopolitical tensions
signals.desc: Brent crude remained above $105 per barrel as escalating Ukraine-Russia energy infrastructure strikes and Middle East tensions support energy prices, pressuring equities.

signals.title: Markets brace for September CPI Wednesday with Fed hike uncertainty
signals.desc: September CPI due Wednesday at 8:30 AM ET with consensus at 3.6-3.7% year-over-year; outcome will shape October 28 Fed decision odds currently at 16-19% for a hike.

verdict: Risk-off tone prevails as chip weakness offsets bank earnings beats, all eyes on Wednesday's CPI for Fed path clarity.
